summary: Add `% raw` ... `% endraw` blocks to SimpleTemplate, so a template can contain text that looks like template code (Vue or Handlebars snippets, docs about stpl) without escaping every line.
behaviour: A line holding only `% raw` opens a raw block and the next line holding only `% endraw` closes it. As with other code lines, either line may be indented and may have spaces after the word, the space after `%` is optional, and with a custom `syntax` the configured line-start token takes the place of `%`.

Everything between the two lines is written to the output exactly as it is, line breaks included: `{{ }}` expressions, `%` lines and `<% %>` blocks inside are not run. The `% raw` and `% endraw` lines write nothing themselves, not even their line break.
A raw block inside a code block, such as between `% if show:` and `% end`, is written only when that code runs.
Only the word `raw` on its own opens a block: lines such as `% raw = 5` or `% raw_html = "<b>"` stay ordinary Python code lines.
A `% raw` with no `% endraw` line after it raises `bottle.StplSyntaxError` when the template is compiled (for example on the first `template()` call).

entries: - Fixed: An empty {{ }} expression raises StplSyntaxError instead of IndexError. (feature/c4d917)
- Changed: SimpleTemplate writes each text block with a single _write() call. (feature/91be3a)

entry: - Added: SimpleTemplate raw blocks (% raw ... % endraw) write their content without running it. ({branch})

main_commits.message: Write template text with one _write() call per block
Raise StplSyntaxError for empty inline expressions
Test that StplParser builds its patterns once per syntax
